books.title: More Baby Animals
books.art_why: Real baby animals exist today, so photographs fit.

pages.text: Do you know what baby animals are called? A baby deer is called a fawn.
pages.brief: A baby deer, a fawn, stands on simple neutral ground in a plain outdoor setting. It faces forward, calm and alert, with its four legs visible and its body shown clearly. The background stays soft and empty so the fawn is the only subject.

pages.text: A baby donkey is called a foal. A baby gorilla is called an infant.
pages.brief: A baby donkey, a foal, stands on simple neutral ground in one plain scene, while a baby gorilla, an infant, sits calmly in another plain soft setting. Both young animals are shown clearly and alone, with empty backgrounds around them.

pages.text: A baby pig is called a piglet. A baby koala is called a joey.
pages.brief: A baby pig, a piglet, stands on simple neutral ground in a plain outdoor setting, while a baby koala, a joey, sits upright in another plain natural setting. Both are shown clearly and calmly, with empty backgrounds and no other animals around.

pages.text: A baby owl is called an owlet. Which other baby animals do you know?
pages.brief: A baby owl, an owlet, sits upright in a plain natural setting, facing forward with a calm expression and its small body shown clearly. The background stays soft and empty, with no other animals or objects around the owlet.

books.title: Apple Tree
books.art_why: Apple trees, seeds, sprouts and blossoms all exist in the real world and can be photographed.

pages.text: An apple grows in a cycle. How does the cycle go?
pages.brief: A single ripe apple hanging on a branch of a leafy apple tree in an orchard, shown as the starting point of a repeating cycle that goes round and round again.

pages.text: First comes the seed.
pages.brief: A close-up of one small brown apple seed lying alone on open soil, the very first thing in the cycle, resting before anything begins to grow.

pages.text: Then comes the sprout.
pages.brief: A tiny green sprout with two small leaves pushing up out of the brown earth where the seed was planted, the second step in the cycle.

pages.text: Next come the years.
pages.brief: The same young apple plant growing taller through season after season, its thin stem reaching upward as the years pass slowly by.

pages.text: Then comes the tree.
pages.brief: A full-grown apple tree standing in an orchard with a thick trunk and a wide leafy crown, the next stage after all those growing years.

pages.text: Next come the blooms.
pages.brief: Close-up branches of the apple tree covered in soft pink and white blossoms opening in spring, the step that comes before the fruit.

pages.text: Then come the apples.
pages.brief: Round red and green apples hanging ripe among the green leaves of the apple tree, ready on the branches after the blossoms have gone.

pages.text: Seeds wait inside each apple. The cycle begins again.
pages.brief: An apple cut open to show the small dark seeds waiting inside, with a whole apple beside it, ready to start the same cycle all over again.

books.title: Animal Costumes
books.art_why: Real dogs, a goat, a cat and a rabbit in costumes exist today and can be photographed

pages.text: People wear costumes. Animals can wear costumes too.
pages.brief: A small group of people stand together wearing colourful costumes, and beside them a real animal is also dressed in a costume. The picture shows plainly that people wear costumes and that animals can wear them too, in a bright, simple setting that is easy for young readers to look at.

pages.text: A dog can wear wings.
pages.brief: A real dog stands calmly wearing a pair of costume wings fitted to its back, the wings spread out on either side like a bird's. The dog looks alert and comfortable, photographed in soft daylight against a plain background so the wings are clear and easy to see.

pages.text: A dog can wear a mane.
pages.brief: A real dog stands wearing a thick costume mane around its neck and head, making it look like a lion. The shaggy fake mane frames the dog's face, and the dog holds still with its ears up, photographed against a plain background in soft, even light.

pages.text: A goat can wear a crown.
pages.brief: A real goat stands wearing a small crown on its head, the shiny points sitting between its ears and horns. The goat looks steady and calm in a simple outdoor setting with soft daylight, and the crown is clearly visible on top of its head.

pages.text: A cat can wear a bandanna.
pages.brief: A real cat sits wearing a patterned bandanna tied around its neck, the cloth hanging down over its chest. The cat looks relaxed with its whiskers forward, photographed in soft daylight against a plain background so the bright bandanna stands out clearly.

pages.text: A dog can wear a mask.
pages.brief: A real dog stands wearing a costume mask over its face, covering the area around its eyes and nose. The dog stays still and calm, its body facing the reader, photographed in even daylight against a simple plain background so the mask is easy to see.

pages.text: A dog can wear fins.
pages.brief: A real dog stands wearing costume fins fitted along its legs and sides, shaped like the fins of a fish. The dog is steady on its feet, photographed in soft daylight against a plain background, with the fins spread out clearly on both sides of its body.

pages.text: A rabbit can wear a hat.
pages.brief: A real rabbit sits upright wearing a small hat on its head, the brim resting between its long ears. The rabbit's nose and whiskers twitch as it stays still, photographed in soft daylight against a plain background so the little hat is easy to see.

pages.text: A dog can wear a snout.
pages.brief: A real dog stands wearing a costume snout fitted over its own nose and muzzle, making its face look longer and different. The dog's ears are up and its eyes are bright, photographed in even daylight against a plain background so the snout stands out clearly.

pages.text: What is this dog wearing?
pages.brief: A real dog stands facing the reader wearing a costume piece, its body still and its ears up. The dog is photographed in soft daylight against a plain background, with the costume item shown large and clear so a young reader can look closely and work out what the dog is wearing.

books.title: What Season Is It?
books.art_why: The book shows real seasons and weather that can be photographed.

pages.text: The leaves change color. When do leaves change color?
pages.brief: Outdoors, a tree stands with leaves in several different colors, showing that the leaves are changing color. The branches hold the leaves as they shift, and the scene focuses on the tree and its changing leaves.

pages.text: Leaves change color in fall.
pages.brief: In a fall scene outdoors, a tree shows leaves that have changed color, with warm-toned leaves on the branches and some fallen leaves on the ground. The setting shows the season of fall, where leaves change color.

pages.text: The snow falls. When does snow fall?
pages.brief: Outdoors, snow falls from the sky in small flakes, drifting down through the air. The scene shows falling snow and the open air around it, illustrating the weather moment when snow is falling.

pages.text: Snow falls in winter.
pages.brief: In a winter scene outdoors, snow falls and covers the ground, with snowflakes coming down through the cold air. The view shows the snowy season of winter, where snow falls, focusing on the falling snow and the winter setting.

pages.text: The flowers grow. When do flowers grow?
pages.brief: Outdoors, flowers grow from the ground, with small green shoots and buds opening upward. The scene focuses on the growing flowers and the soil around them, showing the moment when flowers grow.

pages.text: Flowers grow in spring.
pages.brief: In a spring scene outdoors, flowers grow and bloom, standing in the ground with petals open. The setting shows the season of spring, where flowers grow, and the view centers on the blooming flowers and the ground beneath them.

pages.text: The days become hot. When do days become hot?
pages.brief: Outdoors, the days become hot under a bright sun, with warm light filling the scene. The view shows a hot day with clear, warm air and sunlight, focusing on the heat as the days become hot.

pages.text: Days become hot in summer.
pages.brief: In a summer scene outdoors, the days become hot under strong sunlight, with warm air and bright light across the setting. The view shows the hot season of summer, focusing on the heat and sunlight as the days become hot.

books.title: City Shapes
books.art_why: Real city shapes can be photographed.

pages.text: Look around the city. What shapes do you see?
pages.brief: A simple city scene shows buildings and a street. Different shapes are present around the city for young viewers to notice. The view is open and clear, with the whole city setting visible from one wide angle.

pages.text: Here you see an oval.
pages.brief: In a city setting, one large oval shape is shown clearly. The oval stands apart from the simple city background so it is easy to see. The shape is the main thing to notice, and the surrounding city view stays plain.

pages.text: Here you see triangles.
pages.brief: In a city setting, several triangle shapes are shown together. The triangles stand out clearly against the simple city background. The view stays plain and uncluttered so each triangle can be seen, and the city setting remains easy to notice.

pages.text: Here you see a circle.
pages.brief: In a city setting, one large circle shape is shown clearly. The circle stands out against the simple city background so it is easy to see. The view stays plain, with the circle as the main shape to notice in the city.

pages.text: Here you see squares.
pages.brief: In a city setting, several square shapes are shown together. The squares stand out clearly against the simple city background. The view stays plain and uncluttered so each square can be seen, and the city setting remains easy to notice.

pages.text: Here you see rectangles.
pages.brief: In a city setting, several rectangle shapes are shown together. The rectangles stand out clearly against the simple city background. The view stays plain and uncluttered so each rectangle can be seen, and the city setting remains easy to notice.

pages.text: Here you see hexagons.
pages.brief: In a city setting, several hexagon shapes are shown together. The hexagons stand out clearly against the simple city background. The view stays plain and uncluttered so each hexagon can be seen, and the city setting remains easy to notice.

pages.text: Here you see many shapes. What shapes do you see?
pages.brief: A wide city scene shows many different shapes together. The shapes are spread through the city setting so the whole view is full of them. The scene is clear and open, making the many shapes easy to notice.

books.title: Snow Falls
books.art_why: Snow, mountains, forests, oceans and deserts are real-world scenes best shown in photographs.

pages.text: Snow falls in the mountains.
pages.brief: Wide view of tall mountain peaks under a grey winter sky, with soft snow falling steadily over the rocky slopes and high ridges, settling on the stone and the dark evergreen edges of the mountainside.

pages.text: Snow falls on the plains.
pages.brief: Open flat plains stretch to the horizon under a pale sky, light snow drifting down across the wide grassland and dusting the ground in a thin white layer as far as the eye can see.

pages.text: Snow falls in the forest.
pages.brief: Inside a quiet forest, snow falls between tall trees, resting on branches and trunks, with flakes drifting down through the still air onto the woodland floor below.

pages.text: Snow falls on the ocean.
pages.brief: Snow falls over the open ocean, white flakes drifting down onto the grey-blue water and dissolving into the moving waves, with no land in sight and a pale sky above.

pages.text: Snow falls in the desert.
pages.brief: A desert of sand and scattered rock under a soft sky, with snow falling and beginning to settle in thin white patches across the dry ground and dunes.

pages.text: Snow falls in the winter.
pages.brief: A cold winter scene with bare branches and frosty ground, snow falling steadily through the air and lying deep on the earth in the quiet winter light.

pages.text: Snow falls in the spring.
pages.brief: A spring scene with fresh green shoots and budding branches, light snow falling and landing on the new growth, melting on the softer ground below.

pages.text: Snow falls from the clouds. We fall in the snow!
pages.brief: Grey clouds high above release falling snow, and below, children tumble and play in the deep snow, dropping down into it with arms out, laughing in the cold air.

books.title: Wash Your Hands
books.art_why: Real children washing hands and everyday activities exist in the real world today.

pages.text: Wash your hands before you eat.
pages.brief: A young child sits at a kitchen table with a plate of food ready to eat, hands lifted near the plate, in a bright home kitchen with a grown-up nearby.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you sneeze.
pages.brief: A child sneezes into a bent elbow while standing in a living room, eyes squeezed shut, a tissue box on a low table beside them.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you use the bathroom.
pages.brief: A small child stands at a bathroom sink after using the toilet, reaching toward the tap, with a towel hanging on a nearby rail.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you dig.
pages.brief: A child kneels in a garden digging in dark soil with a small trowel, both hands muddy, grass and plants around them.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you paint.
pages.brief: A child stands at a low table painting with bright colours, fingers dotted with paint, paper and pots of paint in front of them.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you pet a dog.
pages.brief: A child crouches on a floor gently petting a happy dog, one hand on the dog's back, the dog's tail wagging in a sunny room.

pages.text: Wash your hands after you play.
pages.brief: Children play outdoors on a grassy playground, running and laughing together, with a slide and swing frame behind them.

pages.text: Wash front and back. Wash between your fingers, too!
pages.brief: A child washes hands at a sink, rubbing the backs of the hands and between the fingers, soapy bubbles visible, water running from the tap.

books.title: Circles
books.art_why: Real-world subjects like the Sun, flowers, pond, hay, butterfly and tree rings are best shown in photographs.

pages.text: Circles are around the Sun.
pages.brief: A bright, glowing Sun sits in a clear sky, and several round circles are arranged around it. The circles are clearly visible near the Sun, some larger and some smaller, all around the bright center.

pages.text: Circles are in the middle of flowers.
pages.brief: A close-up view of a flower shows round circles in the middle of its petals. The circular center is clearly visible, surrounded by soft petals, and the round shape sits right at the heart of the flower.

pages.text: Circles are on lily pads in a pond.
pages.brief: Lily pads float on the calm surface of a pond, and round circles are visible on the lily pads. The green pads rest on the water, with circular shapes showing clearly on their flat surfaces.

pages.text: Circles are on rolls of hay.
pages.brief: Round rolls of hay sit in a field, with circular shapes visible on their ends. The large hay rolls rest on the ground, and the circles on the rolls of hay are clear and easy to see.

pages.text: Circles are on a butterfly’s wings.
pages.brief: A butterfly rests with its wings spread open, and round circles are visible on the butterfly’s wings. The circular patterns sit clearly on the wings, showing circles right on the butterfly’s wings.

pages.text: Circles are in tree rings.
pages.brief: A cut tree trunk shows circles in tree rings. The rings form round circles across the wood, with each ring making a clear circular line. The circles in the tree rings are easy to see on the cut surface.

pages.text: Do you see circles here?
pages.brief: Several round circles of different sizes appear across the scene, inviting the reader to look closely and find each circle. The picture is filled with circular shapes to spot, and the reader can search for all the circles shown here.

books.title: What Groups Do You See?
books.art_why: Teddy bears and toy animals are real objects that can be photographed.

pages.text: The teddy bears are one group.
pages.brief: A group of teddy bears sits together in one clear area, shown as a single group. The bears are all together, with no other animals mixed in, so the viewer can see the teddy bears as one group.

pages.text: What other groups do you see?
pages.brief: The teddy bears remain in view while other groups are shown nearby. The page does not name these groups; it only asks the viewer to look at the groups present and see what other groups are there.

pages.text: The tiny animals are one group.
pages.brief: A group of tiny animals is shown together in one place. The animals are very small and gathered as one group, separate from the teddy bears, so the viewer can see the tiny animals as a group.

pages.text: What other groups do you see?
pages.brief: The tiny animals are still visible, and other groups are shown nearby for the viewer to find. The page does not name the other groups; it asks the viewer to look at the groups in the picture and see what other groups are there.

pages.text: The animals on the blue pillow are one group.
pages.brief: A group of animals sits together on a blue pillow. The blue pillow holds these animals as one clear group, separate from the teddy bears and the tiny animals, so the viewer can see the animals on the blue pillow as a group.

pages.text: What other groups do you see?
pages.brief: The animals on the blue pillow remain visible, and other groups are shown nearby for the viewer to notice. The page does not name the other groups; it asks the viewer to look at the picture and see what other groups are there.

pages.text: Look at these animals. What other groups could you make?
pages.brief: All the animals are shown together in one view, including the teddy bears, the tiny animals, and the animals on the blue pillow. The page asks the viewer to look at these animals and think about what other groups could be made from them.

books.title: Swamps
books.art_why: Swamps are real natural places that exist today, so photographs fit best.

pages.text: Swamps are areas of wet and dry land.
pages.brief: A wide swamp scene shows wet land and dry land together, with shallow water lying between patches of firm ground. The view is calm and natural, looking across the swamp area from a low outdoor viewpoint. The wet and dry areas are clearly visible in the same landscape.

pages.text: Swamps can have fresh water.
pages.brief: A freshwater swamp scene shows fresh water lying in shallow pools across wet ground. The water is still and clear, filling low areas in the swamp. The view looks across the freshwater swamp in daylight, showing the water and wet ground together.

pages.text: Swamps can have salt water.
pages.brief: A saltwater swamp scene shows salt water lying in shallow pools across wet ground. The water is still, filling low areas near the edge of the swamp. The view looks across the saltwater area in daylight, showing the water and wet ground together.

pages.text: Swamps can have many plants.
pages.brief: A swamp scene shows many plants growing across wet ground. Green plants fill the swamp, standing in shallow water and spreading over the wet land. The view looks across the planted area in daylight, showing plants of different sizes growing together in the swamp.

pages.text: Swamps can have many animals.
pages.brief: A swamp scene shows many animals living among the wet ground and water. Animals are visible in the swamp, moving and resting in the shallow water and on the wet land. The view looks across the busy swamp in daylight, showing animals gathered in the habitat.

pages.text: Swamps help the soil stay healthy.
pages.brief: A swamp scene shows wet ground and soil. The soil looks dark and rich in the swamp, held together by the wet land around it. The view looks closely at the ground in daylight, showing the soil staying healthy within the swamp area.

pages.text: Swamps help the air stay clean.
pages.brief: A swamp scene shows open air above wet ground and water. The air looks clear above the swamp, with the wet land and water spread out below. The view looks across the open swamp in daylight, showing the clean air above the wetland.

pages.text: Swamps help the water stay clean.
pages.brief: A swamp scene shows water lying across wet ground. The water looks clear and clean in shallow pools, resting among the wet land. The view looks across the swamp water in daylight, showing the water staying clean within the swamp area.

pages.text: Swamps help the land stay dry.
pages.brief: A swamp scene shows wet land and dry land beside shallow water. The dry land stays firm above the wet ground, with water held in low areas nearby. The view looks across the swamp in daylight, showing the land staying dry beside the wet areas.

pages.text: Swamps help Earth stay healthy.
pages.brief: A wide view of Earth shows a healthy planet with swamp areas on its surface. The swamps appear among the land and water, helping the whole Earth look healthy. The view looks at Earth from space in daylight, showing the planet staying healthy.

books.title: Ladybugs
books.art_why: Ladybugs are real animals that can be photographed today.

pages.text: All ladybugs are insects.
pages.brief: A close-up view shows several ladybugs as insects, with their small bodies, legs, and antennae visible. They sit together in a simple natural setting, and the picture focuses on their insect shape. The ladybugs are grouped closely so their legs and antennae can be seen.

pages.text: Some ladybugs are red. Some ladybugs are yellow.
pages.brief: Two groups of ladybugs are shown side by side. One group is red, and the other group is yellow. The ladybugs rest in a clear close-up view so their different shell colors are easy to see.

pages.text: Some ladybugs are orange. Some ladybugs are other colors.
pages.brief: A close-up view shows ladybugs in orange and in other colors. One orange ladybug stands out beside ladybugs with different color patterns. They are grouped together so the variety of colors can be seen clearly.

pages.text: Some ladybugs have spots.
pages.brief: Several ladybugs are shown with spots on their wing covers. One ladybug is seen clearly from above, its rounded body marked with small spots. The other spotted ladybugs rest nearby in a simple close-up view.

pages.text: Some ladybugs have stripes.
pages.brief: A close-up view shows ladybugs with stripes on their bodies. The stripes run across their colorful wing covers, and several striped ladybugs rest together in the frame. Their striped markings are clearly visible, so each one can be seen.

pages.text: Some ladybugs have just one color.
pages.brief: A close-up view shows ladybugs that are just one color. Each ladybug has a single solid color across its body, with no spots or stripes visible. Several of these one-color ladybugs rest together in the frame.

pages.text: Some ladybugs eat other insects. Some ladybugs eat plants.
pages.brief: Two ladybugs are shown eating. One ladybug eats another small insect, while another ladybug eats part of a plant. They are seen in a close-up view that shows both kinds of ladybug food. The insect and the plant are clearly visible beside them.

pages.text: All ladybugs have wings.
pages.brief: A ladybug is shown with its wings open. The thin wings spread out from its body, and the ladybug appears ready to fly. A close-up view makes the open wings clearly visible. All ladybugs have wings, and this one shows them spread wide.

books.title: At the Fair
books.art_why: Fairground rides are real places children visit today, so real photographs fit best.

pages.text: You can ride the big wheel.
pages.brief: A tall Ferris wheel with big passenger cars stands at a fairground, rising high against the sky. Children and their families stand below, looking up at the wheel and waiting to climb into one of the cars for a ride.

pages.text: You can ride the little car.
pages.brief: A small colourful car ride spins on its track at the fairground. A young child sits inside one bright little car, holding on and smiling, while other empty cars go round beside it on the ride.

pages.text: You can ride the long train.
pages.brief: A long train ride carries several children in open carriages along a curving track at the fair. The little engine leads the way, and the boys and girls sit in rows, looking ahead as the train moves.

pages.text: You can ride the fast cup.
pages.brief: A spinning teacup ride whirls at the fairground, the cups turning quickly on a round platform. Children sit inside a fast cup, gripping the edge and laughing as it spins round and round.

pages.text: You can ride the painted horse.
pages.brief: A painted carousel horse with bright colours and a decorated saddle stands on the merry-go-round. A child sits on the horse's back, holding the pole, as the carousel goes round at the fair.

pages.text: You can ride the giant swing.
pages.brief: A giant swing ride lifts people high in the air, seats hanging on long chains from a turning top. Children ride the swings, legs dangling, flying out in a wide circle above the fairground.

pages.text: You can ride the tiny plane.
pages.brief: A tiny plane ride circles at the fair, small aircraft painted in bright colours with a child in each seat. One child sits in a little plane, hands on the controls, pretending to fly.

pages.text: What is your favorite ride at the fair?
pages.brief: Children stand together at the busy fairground, looking around at the rides all about them. The big wheel, train and carousel are visible behind them as the friends think about which ride they liked best.

books.title: Spirals, Spirals Everywhere
books.art_why: Horns, shells, plants, fingers, clouds and hair all exist today and photographs show their spirals clearly.

pages.text: A spiral is a shape. A spiral can be found in many things.
pages.brief: One big, clear spiral shape fills the middle of the picture, curling round and round from a tight centre out to a wide open curve. The background is soft and plain so the swirl is easy to follow. Nothing else is in the frame.

pages.text: This horn has a spiral.
pages.brief: A single animal horn, tapering to a point, held up close to the camera. Its surface twists in a long spiral from the wide base to the tip, with ridges catching the light. Warm outdoor light and a plain blurred background.

pages.text: This shell has a spiral.
pages.brief: A seashell resting on damp sand, turning in a tight spiral from a pointed tip round to its opening. Grains of sand and a shallow ripple of water lie nearby, and sea light shines on the shell's ridged surface.

pages.text: This plant has a spiral.
pages.brief: A green plant stem in a garden, its young leaf curled tightly into a spiral as it unfurls. Two or three other leaves spread open behind it. Soft daylight, with soil and stems blurred in the background.

pages.text: This finger has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of a child's finger, held up and turned so the tip faces the viewer. The fine lines on the fingertip swirl round in a clear spiral. Skin and knuckle fill the frame, softly lit.

pages.text: This cloud has a spiral.
pages.brief: A white cloud in a blue sky, its middle curling into a rounded spiral like a swirl of cream. Open sky all around it, with a few small clouds far off near the horizon.

pages.text: This hair has a spiral.
pages.brief: A close-up of thick hair, one curl twisting tightly round into a neat spiral that hangs clear of the rest. The other hair sweeps softly behind it. Warm light and a plain background.

pages.text: A spiral is a shape. Can you find the spirals?
pages.brief: The clear spiral shape from the first page sits big in the middle, with the horn, the shell, the curled leaf, the fingertip, the spiral cloud and the curly hair arranged around it in a ring, all small and easy to spot.

books.title: That's a Fruit?
books.art_why: Real fruits can be clearly photographed for young readers.

pages.text: That’s That’s a Fruit? a Fruit?
pages.brief: A colorful group of whole fruits sits together on a simple surface, inviting a closer look. The fruits are arranged so a young viewer can wonder which ones belong in the fruit group. No people appear in the scene.

pages.text: All fruits have seeds. Some fruits may surprise you.
pages.brief: A group of different fruits rests together, and one or two are cut open so their seeds can be seen inside. The display suggests that seeds are found in fruits, including ones a viewer might not expect. The scene is simple and clear.

pages.text: An avocado is a fruit.
pages.brief: A ripe avocado is shown whole beside a halved avocado with its large seed visible. The avocado sits on a plain, light surface, presented clearly as a fruit. No people or other objects are in the scene.

pages.text: An eggplant is a fruit.
pages.brief: A shiny purple eggplant is shown whole and also cut open to reveal its seeds inside. It rests on a plain, light surface, presented clearly as a fruit for a young reader. The picture keeps the focus on the eggplant alone.

pages.text: Can you name some other surprising fruits?
pages.brief: A varied group of surprising fruits is arranged in a bright, inviting display, with space around them as if inviting a viewer to name them. The fruits are shown clearly and simply. No people are present.

books.title: What Animals Eat
books.art_why: Real animals eating real food can be shown in photographs.

pages.text: Cows like to eat grass. Munch, munch. Birds like to eat seeds. Crunch, crunch.
pages.brief: On a grassy farm field, a cow stands with its head down, munching green grass. Nearby, a small bird pecks at scattered seeds on the ground, crunching them. Both animals are eating in a sunny outdoor setting.

pages.text: Pandas like to eat leaves. Munch, munch. Frogs like to eat bugs. Zap, zap.
pages.brief: A panda sits among leafy green bamboo, slowly chewing leaves. Beside a small pond, a frog flicks out its tongue to catch tiny bugs, zapping them. The two animals are eating in a quiet nature scene.

pages.text: Monkeys like to eat fruit. Slurp, slurp. Seals like to eat fish. Gulp, gulp.
pages.brief: A lively monkey perches on a tree branch, slurping juicy fruit. In cold blue water, a seal catches and swallows a whole fish with a gulp. Both animals are busy eating their food in their own wild habitats.

pages.text: Goats like to eat everything. Hey, stop! That’s my sock. Hey, stop! That’s my shoe. Hey, stop! That’s my book.
pages.brief: A goat stands in a yard, nibbling a sock, a shoe and a book. A surprised child nearby calls out to stop the goat from eating the child's things. The goat keeps munching anyway.

books.title: Strange Animals
books.art_why: Strange animals are real living things, so photographs fit.

pages.text: Animals are living things. Some animals look strange.
pages.brief: The page shows several animals as living things, grouped in a clear view so each can be seen. A few of the animals have odd, unusual bodies that make them look strange, while all are presented as real creatures.

pages.text: A panda ant looks strange.
pages.brief: A panda ant is shown as a real living creature. Its body is presented clearly so its strange appearance can be seen, and it is the only animal on the page. The view is simple and close enough to notice its unusual look.

pages.text: A blue dragon looks strange.
pages.brief: A blue dragon is shown as a real living creature. It appears alone in a clear, simple view, with its body visible so its strange appearance stands out. The picture keeps the focus on this unusual animal and nothing else.

pages.text: A star spider looks strange.
pages.brief: A star spider is shown as a real living creature. It sits alone in a clear, simple view, with its body visible so its strange appearance can be noticed. The picture keeps the focus on this unusual animal.

pages.text: A turtle frog looks strange.
pages.brief: A turtle frog is shown as a real living creature. It appears alone in a clear, simple view, with its body visible so its strange appearance stands out. The picture keeps the focus on this unusual animal and nothing else.

pages.text: A rosy moth looks strange.
pages.brief: A rosy moth is shown as a real living creature. It appears alone in a clear, simple view, with its body visible so its strange appearance can be seen. The picture keeps the focus on this unusual animal.

pages.text: A water bear looks strange.
pages.brief: A water bear is shown as a real living creature. It appears alone in a clear, simple view, with its body visible so its strange appearance stands out. The picture keeps the focus on this unusual animal and nothing else.

pages.text: Do these animals look strange?
pages.brief: The page shows a group of the strange animals from the book, all presented as real living creatures. They are gathered in a clear view, and their unusual appearances are easy to compare so viewers can decide whether they look strange.

books.title: Ice
books.art_why: Ice, water, houses, fences and cars are everyday real things a camera can show.

pages.text: Ice forms when water gets cold and freezes.
pages.brief: A close-up photograph of a shallow puddle of water in the open air on a cold day, the clear water turning solid and glassy at its edges as it freezes into a smooth sheet of ice.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet house.
pages.brief: A house seen from outside on a cold morning, its walls and window frames wet and shiny, with a thin clear layer of ice forming over the damp surfaces and glinting in the pale light.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet fence.
pages.brief: A wooden fence outdoors, its rails darkened and wet from damp weather, with a thin shiny coating of ice spreading across the wet wood and shining along the top edges.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet car.
pages.brief: A car parked outdoors on a cold day, its wet roof, windows and doors covered with a thin clear layer of ice that shines and reflects the pale sky.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet road.
pages.brief: A wet road surface outdoors, dark and damp, with a smooth clear sheet of ice forming across the wet asphalt and catching the cold light.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet sign.
pages.brief: A sign standing outdoors beside a path, its surface wet from damp weather, with a thin clear coating of ice forming over the wet face and edges of the sign.

pages.text: Ice can form on a wet sidewalk.
pages.brief: A wet sidewalk outdoors, the paving damp and dark, with a thin shiny layer of ice forming across the wet concrete and gleaming where the light hits it.

pages.text: Ice can be very slippery!
pages.brief: A close view of a smooth sheet of ice on the ground, glassy and slick, shining with a hard bright surface that looks dangerously slippery underfoot.

books.title: Animals That Sting
books.art_why: These are real animals alive today, so real photographs are possible.

pages.text: Some animals sting to defend themselves. Stings can hurt.
pages.brief: A close view of a stinging animal in a natural outdoor setting, its stinging part clearly visible as it defends itself, showing that a sting can hurt.

pages.text: This bee stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A striped bee in a garden, wings raised and stinger pushed out as it defends itself, resting on a green leaf in warm daylight.

pages.text: This jellyfish stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A jellyfish floating in blue sea water, its long tentacles trailing down as it defends itself, seen from close by in the ocean.

pages.text: This worm stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A segmented marine worm on wet sand and shallow water, its body curled as it defends itself, small bristles showing along its sides.

pages.text: This ray stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A ray lying flat on a sandy seabed in clear shallow water, its tail raised with the stinging spine visible as it defends itself.

pages.text: This ant stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: An ant standing on dry ground, its body angled up and stinger showing at the back as it defends itself in a sunny outdoor setting.

pages.text: This wasp stings to defend itself.
pages.brief: A wasp with bright yellow and black stripes clinging to a leaf, its stinger pointed out as it defends itself in a garden.

pages.text: Stings can help keep animals safe.
pages.brief: A stinging animal resting safely in its natural surroundings, its stinging part ready, showing how a sting can help keep an animal safe.

books.title: Airplanes
books.art_why: Airplanes are real machines that exist today.

pages.text: Airplanes are amazing machines.
pages.brief: A large silver passenger airplane rests on a sunny airport runway, with a smaller white propeller plane parked nearby. Both aircraft have wings spread wide and shine in the daylight. The runway stretches behind them toward a clear blue sky.

pages.text: People use airplanes to get things.
pages.brief: A big cargo airplane sits at an airport with its side door open. Workers in bright vests lift cardboard boxes and stacked packages up a ramp into the plane. More boxes wait on the tarmac. The airplane's nose and wings fill the background.

pages.text: People use airplanes to go places.
pages.brief: A family walks up metal stairs to board a white passenger airplane at a sunny airport. A parent carries a bag while children follow close behind. The airplane's open door waits at the top. A blue sky and airport buildings are behind them.

pages.text: People use airplanes to put out fires.
pages.brief: A red and white firefighting airplane flies low over a smoky forest fire. A long stream of water pours from its belly toward the flames below. Tall trees stand in the smoke, and the sky is hazy with gray clouds.

pages.text: People use airplanes to help grow food.
pages.brief: A small yellow crop-dusting airplane flies low over a green farm field. Fine mist sprays from the wings behind it, drifting over rows of young crops. The field stretches to a line of trees under a bright sky.

pages.text: People use airplanes to do tricks.
pages.brief: A red aerobatic airplane loops high in a clear blue sky, leaving a long white smoke trail. The plane is tilted sideways, showing its wings and tail. The smoke curls in a wide arc behind it, with no clouds around.

pages.text: People use airplanes to have fun.
pages.brief: Children and parents sit on a grassy field at an airshow, looking up and smiling. A colorful small airplane flies overhead, trailing white smoke. Families have picnic blankets and bags beside them. The sky is bright and clear.

pages.text: People use airplanes in many ways.
pages.brief: A busy airport shows airplanes in many roles: a passenger jet at a gate, a cargo plane being loaded, and a small propeller plane on the runway. In the distance, another airplane climbs into a blue sky over airport buildings.

books.title: What Does the Wind Move?
books.art_why: Wind, sailboats, balloons, windmills, kites and shirts are real things that can be photographed.

pages.text: The wind moves many things. The wind pushes a sailboat.
pages.brief: A sailboat on open water, its sail filled and curved by a strong wind. The wind pushes against the sail, moving the boat forward across the water. The focus is on the sailboat and the windy air around it.

pages.text: The wind carries a balloon. The wind floats a bag.
pages.brief: A balloon floats through the air, carried along by the wind. Nearby, a bag drifts and floats as the same wind lifts it. The scene shows the balloon, the bag and the windy air around them, with the wind carrying both objects along.

pages.text: The wind turns a windmill. The wind lifts a kite.
pages.brief: A windmill stands outdoors, its blades turning as the wind pushes them around. Above, a kite rises and lifts in the same wind, its string taut. The scene shows the windmill turning and the kite lifting, with the wind acting on both.

pages.text: The wind blows a shirt. The wind moves many things. It is always moving something!
pages.brief: A shirt hangs outdoors and blows in the wind, its fabric rippling and flapping. The windy air moves the shirt and continues moving things around it. The scene focuses on the shirt in the wind, showing that the wind is always moving something.

books.title: So Many Fish
books.art_why: Real fish with these colours and shapes exist today.

pages.text: This fish is silver and shiny.
pages.brief: A single fish with a silver body and shiny scales is shown. Light catches the shiny surface, making the fish look bright. The fish is the only subject, presented close and clear so its silver colour and glossy shine are easy to see.

pages.text: This fish is blue and bright.
pages.brief: A single fish with a bright blue body is shown. Its blue colour looks strong and clear, and its fins and body stand out in the picture. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the bright blue shade is easy to notice.

pages.text: This fish is red and scary.
pages.brief: A single fish with a red body is shown. The red colour gives it a scary look, and its shape seems bold and alarming. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the strong red colour and scary appearance are easy to see.

pages.text: This fish is brown and pointy.
pages.brief: A single fish with a brown body is shown. Its body and fins look pointy, giving the fish a sharp, angular appearance. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the brown colour and pointy shape are easy to notice.

pages.text: This fish is black and spotted.
pages.brief: A single fish with a black body and spots is shown. The dark body is covered with spotted markings, making the fish easy to recognise. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the black colour and spotted pattern are clear.

pages.text: This fish is yellow and boxy.
pages.brief: A single fish with a yellow body is shown. Its body has a boxy shape, with a squared look rather than a smooth curve. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the yellow colour and boxy form are easy to see.

pages.text: This fish is orange and striped.
pages.brief: A single fish with an orange body and stripes is shown. The orange colour is marked with stripes along its body, making the fish stand out. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the orange colour and striped pattern are clear.

pages.text: This fish is gold and puffy.
pages.brief: A single fish with a gold body is shown. Its body looks puffy and rounded, giving the fish a soft, swollen shape. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the gold colour and puffy form are easy to see.

pages.text: This fish is purple and fancy.
pages.brief: A single fish with a purple body is shown. Its fins and body look fancy, with an elaborate, decorative appearance. The fish is the main subject, shown close so the purple colour and fancy shape are easy to notice.

pages.text: So many fish swim in the sea!
pages.brief: Many fish are shown swimming together in the sea. The fish fill the water, moving as a large group. The sea is around them, and the many fish swimming together are the main subject of the picture.

books.title: Tools
books.art_why: Every tool named—pencil, rake, hammer, shovel, knife and wheelbarrow—is a real object that exists today and can be photographed.

pages.text: I see tools everywhere. Tools help us work. Here is a tool. It is a pencil for writing.
pages.brief: A single sharpened wooden pencil with a pink eraser lies diagonally on a plain light wooden surface. Its dark grey tip points toward the lower corner, and soft daylight falls across the smooth tabletop, showing the pencil clearly as a tool for writing.

pages.text: Here is a tool. It is a rake for raking. Here is a tool. It is a hammer for pounding.
pages.brief: A long-handled rake with metal tines stands on short green grass, its teeth resting on the lawn. Beside it, a claw hammer with a wooden handle and steel head lies on a plain wooden workbench, ready for pounding.

pages.text: Here is a tool. It is a shovel for digging. Here is a tool. It is a knife for cutting.
pages.brief: A sturdy shovel with a metal blade and a wooden handle stands upright in loose brown soil. Next to it, a kitchen knife with a silver blade and a dark handle lies flat on a plain wooden surface, its edge ready for cutting.

pages.text: Here is a tool. It is a wheelbarrow for carrying. I see tools everywhere. What tools do you see?
pages.brief: A green wheelbarrow with one front wheel, two handles and a deep tray sits on a patch of short grass. Its tray is empty and clean, and the wheelbarrow rests steady in the open garden, a tool made for carrying.

books.title: The Animals of Canada
books.art_why: All the animals are real and exist in Canada today, so photographs fit.

pages.text: This is a moose. It lives in Canada. This is a goose. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: A large moose with broad antlers stands at the edge of a northern lake in Canada, tall pine trees behind it. Nearby, a Canada goose with a black neck and white cheek patch stands on the grassy shore, facing the water.

pages.text: This is a bear. It lives in Canada. This is a beaver. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: A black bear walks through a Canadian forest clearing among evergreen trees, head low as it moves. On a muddy bank in a Canadian wetland, a brown beaver with a flat tail sits upright, front paws held close.

pages.text: This is an eagle. It lives in Canada. This is a wolf. It lives in Canada.
pages.brief: A bald eagle with a white head and dark wings perches on a high tree branch in Canada, looking out over the land. Below, a grey wolf stands in a grassy Canadian clearing, ears alert, facing forward.

pages.text: This is a loon. It lives in Canada. Many animals live in Canada.
pages.brief: A loon with a black-and-white patterned neck floats on a calm Canadian lake, small ripples around it. Across the far shore and forest edge, many Canadian animals gather, including a moose, bear, beaver, eagle, wolf and goose.

books.title: Rocks
books.art_why: Mountains, boulders, stones, pebbles, sand and dust all exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: This is a mountain.
pages.brief: A tall mountain rising against the sky, its rocky slopes and ridges stretching upward. Grey and brown stone covers the mountain from the wide base to the high peak, with a few small clouds drifting past behind it.

pages.text: A mountain is made of rock.
pages.brief: A close view of the mountain's side, showing the solid rock it is made of. Rough grey stone forms the cliff face, with cracks and layers running through it, filling the whole picture from top to bottom.

pages.text: This is a boulder. It broke off the mountain.
pages.brief: A big rounded boulder lying on the ground at the foot of the mountain. A fresh broken patch shows where it came apart from the mountain rock above it, and smaller pieces of rubble rest nearby on the ground.

pages.text: This is a stone. It broke off the boulder.
pages.brief: A hand-sized stone sitting on the ground beside the much larger boulder. The stone has a rough broken edge where it split away from the boulder, and bits of grit lie scattered around it on the bare earth.

pages.text: This is a pebble. It broke off the stone.
pages.brief: A small smooth pebble resting on the ground next to the stone it came from. The pebble is tiny compared with the stone, with a broken face where it snapped off, and dry ground spreads out around them.

pages.text: This is sand. It broke off the pebble.
pages.brief: A close view of a pebble crumbling into loose grains of sand. The little heap of sand spreads out on the ground where the pebble broke apart, with individual pale grains visible in the pile.

pages.text: This is dust.
pages.brief: An extreme close view of fine dust lying on a flat surface. The dust is a thin scattering of tiny grey and brown specks, much smaller than sand grains, resting lightly on the ground.

pages.text: Dust is the tiniest piece of rock. Dust is everywhere.
pages.brief: Fine dust settling on everyday surfaces: a windowsill, a tabletop and a shelf, each holding a thin film of tiny specks. The dust lies in the air and on the surfaces around a simple room.

books.title: Making Salsa!
books.art_why: Making salsa is a real everyday kitchen activity with real ingredients.

pages.text: In go the peppers. 4 In goes the onion.
pages.brief: A young child in a kitchen adds chopped peppers into a bowl on the counter, then drops pieces of onion in after them. The child's hands work over the bowl, peppers and onion pieces going in one after the other.

pages.text: In goes the tomato. 6 In goes the salt.
pages.brief: The same young child tips a chopped tomato into the bowl on the kitchen counter, then sprinkles salt from a small dish into the bowl. The child leans over the bowl, adding the tomato and the salt in turn.

pages.text: In goes the black pepper. 8 In goes the cilantro.
pages.brief: In the kitchen, the young child shakes black pepper into the bowl and then adds fresh cilantro leaves, dropping them in. The child's hands hover over the bowl as the pepper and the cilantro go in.

pages.text: In goes the lemon juice. I mix the salsa. We eat chips and salsa!
pages.brief: The young child squeezes lemon juice into the bowl and mixes the salsa with a spoon. Then the child sits at a table with a bowl of chips, eating chips and salsa.
